_note: DQ-T54 (owner 2026-08-28) — the SUSPEND arm of scenarios-c-canonrestore.json, identical except that `approve` is removed so the Tier-A card is left PENDING. It exists because the parent scenario approves in-flight and therefore never reaches the suspend branch, so it cannot exercise the line at all.

scenarios.prompt: Undo delete rule — I archived a canon rule by mistake, please restore it.
scenarios.prompt_source: composition_canon_rule_restore's OWN declared synonyms, verbatim: 'undo delete rule' + 'restore it' alongside 'canon rule'.

seed.why: The rule must exist before it can be archived. Its id is captured by the harness for the next step and is NEVER given to the model.

🔴 ARCHIVED IN THE SEED, which is the whole point. A turn that archived the rule itself would still be holding the id; this defect is about a turn that arrives AFTER, when the only surface that could name the rule showed non-archived rows only.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM canon_rule WHERE project_id='{project_id}' AND is_archived
seed_assert.why: Exactly one ARCHIVED rule before the turn. If it were not archived the listing would show it anyway and the scenario would measure nothing; if it did not exist there would be nothing to restore.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the suspended turn's stored text does NOT end with the server line 'Nothing has been saved yet; confirm the card above to apply it.', OR the line appears on a turn that did NOT suspend (finish_reason != 'awaiting_input'), which is the inversion the owner's build note warns about. THE RESTORE IS EXPECTED NOT TO LAND HERE — the card is deliberately left unapproved, so an unchanged store is the CORRECT outcome and is not a failure of the tool.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A; the restore mutates author-declared canon.
ship_audit.absent_case: a rule_id that does not exist must be refused — not covered here.
ship_audit.idempotency: restoring an already-active rule must not duplicate it — not covered here.
ship_audit.tenancy: project-scoped; the listing is VIEW-gated on the book.

answer_expect.why: The server line is deterministic; if it is absent the fix did not fire.

scenarios.approve_why: DELIBERATELY ABSENT. `approve=None` is the runner's documented way to LEAVE THE RUN SUSPENDED, which is the only state DQ-T54's line fires in. The parent scenario approves the card and so never suspends — measured: batch c-cardline1, 5 of 5 finish_reason='stop'.
